channel.title: NRBC Compliance Brief
channel.description: A daily morning brief from New Realm Brewing on alcohol and hemp/THC regulation — TTB and state actions, hemp THC beverage rules, tariffs, court decisions and enforcement. Federal and all 50 states.

item.title: Illinois hemp THC restrictions now in effect — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 91 (Nov 12, 2026)
item.description: Illinois hemp THC restrictions take effect today; most sales move to dispensaries only. Also: DEA rejects medical cannabis business registrations in at least six states and D.C; Senate appropriators encourage hemp cultivar development, raise cannabinoid-food concerns

item.title: Illinois hemp ban takes effect Thursday for most — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 90 (Nov 11, 2026)
item.description: Illinois hemp THC ban takes effect Thursday for businesses outside the lawsuit pause. Also: Beer Institute puts aluminum, taxes and hemp at center of agenda for new Congress; Texas Democrats prefile marijuana legalization bills for 2027 session

item.title: Illinois pauses hemp enforcement for 250 businesses — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 89 (Nov 10, 2026)
item.description: Illinois agrees to pause hemp THC enforcement for about 250 businesses until Nov. 19. Also: Congressional researchers say FDA is nine months late on required hemp cannabinoid lists and "container" guidance; DEA proposes 2027 marijuana production quotas, with separate Schedule III limits to follow

item.title: Illinois hemp sellers ask court to halt ban — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 88 (Nov 9, 2026)
item.description: Illinois hemp businesses ask federal court to halt THC ban days before Thursday deadline. Also: Tribal group asks DOJ to amend rescheduling order to cover tribally licensed cannabis; South Carolina's consumable THC market braces for Dec. 11 federal limits

item.title: Texas court resets hemp fee case for 2027 — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 87 (Nov 8, 2026)
item.description: Texas appeals court cancels hemp-rules arguments after Democratic justices win election. Also: DEA and rescheduling opponents file final briefs as Schedule III hearing record closes; Illinois businesses race Wednesday deadline to pull hemp THC drinks; trade group seeks emergency court order

item.title: Illinois THC drinks must exit shelves Wednesday — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 86 (Nov 7, 2026)
item.description: Illinois businesses face Wednesday deadline to pull hemp THC drinks as breweries sell down stock. Also: December 11 hemp deadline holds as officials and industry stake out positions after the midterms; Missouri AG promises more retailer lawsuits as judge lets state hemp ban stand

item.title: Missouri sues retailers over marijuana sold as hemp — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 85 (Nov 6, 2026)
item.description: Missouri sues four retailers over alleged marijuana-as-hemp sales as federal court upholds state hemp law. Also: Illinois leaders ask new Congress to let the federal hemp THC ban take effect without further delay; Minnesota opens 2027 hemp license applications with a revised fee schedule

item.title: Democrats take Congress, cannabis policy outlook shifts — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 84 (Nov 5, 2026)
item.description: Democrats take both chambers of Congress, putting the federal cannabis and hemp agenda in new hands. Also: Senator-elect Talarico says he will work with the White House on federal cannabis legalization; Pennsylvania poised to legalize marijuana as Democrats claim state Senate majority

item.title: Massachusetts voters reject retail cannabis repeal — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 83 (Nov 4, 2026)
item.description: Massachusetts voters reject Question 8; retail cannabis sales to remain legal. Also: Hemp law's synthetic-cannabinoid provisions take effect Nov. 12; broader THC redefinition follows Dec. 11; Georgia raises medical cannabis card fee from $30 to $75, effective Dec. 5

item.title: Massachusetts votes today on retail cannabis repeal — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 82 (Nov 3, 2026)
item.description: Massachusetts voters decide today whether to end retail cannabis sales. Also: AMA urges FDA to keep botanical-drug decisions science-based, proposes cannabis research schedule; Local alcohol and cannabis questions fill today's midterm ballots

item.title: Massachusetts votes on ending retail marijuana sales — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 81 (Nov 2, 2026)
item.description: Massachusetts votes Tuesday on ending retail marijuana sales statewide. Also: Denver judge keeps Coors–Constellation distribution deal in place pending arbitration; Alabama regulators: two more medical cannabis dispensaries open this week, five statewide

item.title: Alcohol lobbyists urged AGs to keep hemp ban — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 80 (Nov 1, 2026)
item.description: Report: Alcohol company lobbyists urged state attorneys general to back federal hemp THC limits. Also: Cannabis businesses await IRS guidance on deductions after rescheduling; DEA posts daily-updated list of nearly 7,000 rescheduling applicants

item.title: DEA issues first marijuana dispensary registrations — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 79 (Oct 31, 2026)
item.description: DEA issues first federal registrations to more than 900 medical marijuana dispensaries. Also: DEA sets Nov. 29 deadline for registered businesses to build compliant supply chains; House bill would add a 50% tariff and import testing to China-origin cannabinoid products

item.title: Senators ask USPS to refuse cannabis deliveries — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 78 (Oct 30, 2026)
item.description: Senators ask USPS to stay out of Georgia's medical cannabis delivery plan. Also: House bill would rewrite the Controlled Substances Act and deschedule marijuana; Michigan bill would pause new 24% wholesale marijuana tax for one year

item.title: Illinois retailers wind down THC drink sales — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 77 (Oct 29, 2026)
item.description: Illinois retailers wind down THC drink sales ahead of Nov. 12 reclassification. Also: DEA prepares to publish list of cannabis businesses seeking federal protections under rescheduling; Vermont CBD producers reformulate and resize products ahead of federal THC cap

item.title: Lawmaker floats reconciliation path to avert hemp ban — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 76 (Oct 28, 2026)
item.description: Griffith proposes putting hemp THC rules in a post-election reconciliation bill. Also: Rhode Island details hemp quarantine terms: inventory reports due Dec. 4, no sales after Dec. 11; South Dakota finalizes 35 medical marijuana rule changes, effective Nov. 5

item.title: Illinois sets hemp retailer rules for Nov. 12 — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 75 (Oct 27, 2026)
item.description: Illinois Revenue Department sets retailer compliance steps for the Nov. 12 hemp overhaul. Also: OMB clears streamlined USDA hemp production survey; Massachusetts House leader defends state-run liquor licensing after auditor urges overhaul

item.title: House bill offers brewers spent-grain tax credit — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 74 (Oct 26, 2026)
item.description: Bipartisan House bill would give brewers an excise tax credit for donated spent grain. Also: Booker presses DEA on employee-conviction rules for registering dispensaries; New Jersey hemp-drink extension is one Assembly vote from passage

item.title: Texas hemp groups sue over THCA rule, fees — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 73 (Oct 25, 2026)
item.description: Texas hemp groups sue DSHS over THCA rule and sharply higher license fees. Also: UPS to require THC testing documentation on hemp shipments starting Dec. 11; Virginia Senate finance chair indicted on federal marijuana and racketeering charges

item.title: DEA registration staffing rules draw Senate criticism — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 72 (Oct 24, 2026)
item.description: DEA registration rules force staffing choices at marijuana retailers seeking Schedule III protections. Also: Oklahoma's top medical marijuana regulator steps down; compliance chief named interim director; Minnesota opens $10.9 million CanRenew grant round; businesses among eligible applicants
